subject: FinBank — Deployment & data residency follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sven Lauber <sven.lauber@finbank.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: FinBank — Deployment & data residency follow-up

Hi Sven —

Great speaking earlier today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for FinBank: Hosted API (regional), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in a cloud region), or Private (VPC / on-prem).

Key points I captured:
- Data residency requirement: FinBank needs customer data and audit logs to remain within the EU for production workloads.
- Latency: internal apps are EU-only today; APAC traffic is not in scope for this phase.
- Compliance: Procurement will want SOC 2 evidence and details on network egress/ingress logging.

How each option maps to your needs:
1) Hosted (recommended for speed to value) — We can provision Hosted endpoints restricted to our EU regions (we typically keep data at rest and primary processing within eu-west-1/eu-west-2 depending on customer preference). Cross-region failover is available but only if you opt-in; by default traffic and logs remain in-region.
2) Dedicated — Reserved GPU pools in an EU region, isolated tenant capacity. Good for predictable throughput and stronger tenancy boundaries; still managed by Redwood but we can restrict all runtime and logs to the chosen EU region.
3) Private (VPC or on-prem) — Full network control (customer-managed VPC peering or air-gapped on-prem install). This gives you the strongest guarantee that no customer data leaves your environment.

Attachments I’m sharing: eu-region-capacity-options.pdf (quick breakdown of region options + latency characteristics), redwood-security-overview.pdf, and a mutual-action-plan.xlsx to capture timelines and milestones.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep-dive with your infra/security lead (30–45m) to validate network/firewall requirements and SSO/KMS integration.
- Decision: Hosted EU vs Dedicated vs Private based on residency + cost + SLA tradeoffs.

Are you available for a technical call on Tue/Wed next week? I can bring our infra lead (Dylan Brooks) and Marissa from Compliance.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachments: eu-region-capacity-options.pdf (3 pages), redwood-security-overview.pdf (8 pages), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (1 sheet)

From: Sven Lauber <sven.lauber@finbank.eu>

Cc: procurement@finbank.eu
Date: 19 Oct 2026 11:08:00 +0200
Subject: Re: FinBank — Deployment & data residency follow-up

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the recap and the docs. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing:
- Residency is a hard requirement: all customer data (including index/data at rest) and audit logs must remain in the EU. Temporary caching outside the EU is not acceptable.
- Cross-region routing: we need to understand how failover works. If Hosted endpoints will ever route traffic outside the EU during failover, that is a blocker for Hosted unless we can lock-in EU-only routing.
- Latency: not a primary concern for this phase (EU-only), but we need SLA numbers and expected p95 latency for both Hosted EU and Dedicated in our region.
- Procurement asks: SOC 2 Type II report, network architecture diagram, and a redlined SOW for Dedicated/Private pricing.

Also please include rough cost delta between Dedicated and Private (order-of-magnitude is fine) and expected lead time to stand up Dedicated capacity in an EU region.

Can we do the technical call on Wednesday afternoon CET? Procurement would like to be on the call as well.

Regards,
Sven Lauber
Head of Infrastructure
FinBank
Sven.Lauber@finbank.eu

--
Attachment: FinBank_SOC2_questions.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sven Lauber <sven.lauber@finbank.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 20 Oct 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FinBank — Deployment & data residency follow-up

Sven — thanks, appreciate the clear constraints. Quick answers inline (and next steps):

On residency:
- Hosted EU: we can guarantee that production data at rest and logs are stored in the chosen EU region. We do not perform caching to non-EU regions for production workflows unless explicitly configured for global failover. We are happy to include a contractual clause to lock EU-only routing for your tenant if that’s required.

On cross-region failover:
- By default Hosted endpoints do not route outside the tenant region. Cross-region failover is an opt-in policy; we can disable it entirely for your organization. If you enable it, we can restrict failover targets to EU regions only.

On Dedicated vs Private lead times and costs (ballpark):
- Dedicated: typically 2–4 weeks lead time to provision reserved GPU pools in an EU region for a standard capacity profile. Monthly committed pricing is in the low-mid six figures depending on vGPU capacity and throughput requirements — I’ll share a more exact estimate after we define the target qps/seq length.
- Private (VPC peering): 4–8 weeks to configure depending on network approvals; on-prem install add-on can be longer (8–12 weeks) and requires deeper ops support. Private is higher capex/contract cost but gives you the strongest residency/control guarantees.

Attachments I’m sending: updated mutual-action-plan.xlsx (schedules + milestones) and a SOW template + SSO/KMS integration checklist.

For the technical call on Wednesday afternoon CET — that works. Proposed agenda:
1) Residency & routing (Sven + Procurement)
2) Network/firewall requirements (Dylan + FinBank infra)
3) KMS/keys and audit log flow (Marissa + Security)
4) Timeline & pricing next steps

Would you and procurement be ok with Wed 21 Oct at 15:00 CET?

Best,
Aditya

--
Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (updated), SOW_template.docx, sso-kms-checklist.pdf
